slot.brief: Loop with changing area or entering/leaving a field region as per diagram; compute induced emf via dΦ/dt

stem: A square loop of side $20\ \text{cm}$ enters a region of uniform magnetic field $B = 0.5\ \text{T}$ directed perpendicular to its plane at a constant speed of $2\ \text{m s}^{-1}$, as shown in the figure. The magnitude of the induced emf in the loop while it is entering the field is:

verdicts.working: While entering, flux changes at rate dΦ/dt = B·L·v with L the side cutting the boundary. emf = B L v = 0.5 × 0.20 × 2 = 0.2 V.

working:
The magnetic flux linked with the loop at any time $t$ while entering the magnetic field is given by:
$$\Phi = B A(t) = B (l x)$$
where $l = 20\ \text{cm} = 0.2\ \text{m}$ is the side length of the loop and $x$ is the length of the loop that has entered the field.

According to Faraday's law of electromagnetic induction, the magnitude of the induced emf is:
$$|\mathcal{E}| = \left|\dfrac{d\Phi}{dt}\right| = B l \dfrac{dx}{dt} = B l v$$

Substituting the given values:
$$|\mathcal{E}| = 0.5\ \text{T} \times 0.2\ \text{m} \times 2\ \text{m s}^{-1} = 0.2\ \text{V}$$

Independent check: While entering, flux changes at rate dΦ/dt = B·L·v with L the side cutting the boundary. emf = B L v = 0.5 × 0.20 × 2 = 0.2 V.

draft.distractor_notes:
Option A ($0.04\ \text{V}$) comes from mistakenly computing $B A v = B l^2 v$, confusing side length $l$ with area $A$.
Option B ($0.1\ \text{V}$) comes from including an incorrect factor of $1/2$ (e.g., confusing with the formula for a rotating rod, $\frac{1}{2} B \omega l^2$).
Option D ($0.4\ \text{V}$) comes from doubling the result ($2 B l v$), wrongly assuming both vertical arms contribute constructively.

figure.description: A vertical dashed line divides the plane into two regions: a field-free region on the left and a magnetic field region on the right. In the right region, a uniform magnetic field directed perpendicularly into the page is represented by a grid of '×' symbols and labeled '$B = 0.5\ \text{T}$'. A square conducting loop with side length labeled '$20\ \text{cm}$' lies in the plane of the page and is partially across the dashed boundary, entering the field region. A horizontal arrow pointing to the right is attached to the loop and labeled '$v = 2\ \text{m s}^{-1}$'.
